scope_decisions: Open as a separate cycle, not as a follow-up commit on rec-c3.3-train-a. The pre-existing failures belong to the baseline, not to Tren A.

Slice A: REC-C1.5.2 (commit 3cc511ef) deliberately established strict / fail-closed replay semantics — corruption => ReplayIntegrity, no implicit salvage, no invented Gap. The stale test comment 'First segment is skipped; second segment still recovers' is the symptom; the fix is to reconcile the test (and any docstring) with the strict semantics, NOT to revert REC-C1.5.2.

Slice A scope explicitly excludes changing the production replay semantics. If, during reconciliation, evidence appears that contradicts REC-C1.5.2 (e.g. an authoritative source documents lenient replay as the correct semantics for this case), the cycle must STOP and report back; the change becomes REC-C1.5.3 scope.
Slice B: the harness / coverage integration is broken; the six tests themselves are not. Fix the harness. NO #[ignore]. NO --skip. NO exclusion patterns added to reconstruction-contracts.toml.
Slice C: each pre-existing drift finding gets a concrete owner (cycle + slice). The Vault Drift Sweep must reach exit 0 by reconciliation, not by hiding drift.

No code change in chronos-native, chronos-log, chronos-services, chronos-store, chronos-mcp that touches REC-C3 hexagonal seam, capability-bundle ports, or REC-C1.5.2 replay semantics. This cycle is pure hygiene.
No tag. This is a hygiene cycle, not a behavior-bumping cycle.

slices_executed.title: fix(services): split PositionBeforeRetention into typed ServiceError::CursorStale
slices_executed.rationale: The canonical-evidence translator collapsed ExecutionLogError::PositionBeforeRetention into the opaque ServiceError::DrainFailed via a wildcard arm, hiding the typed ServiceError::CursorStale { requested_next_seq, retained_from_seq } that the port was defined to surface and that chronos-sandbox::restart_uat::r2_stale_cursor expects. Regression was masked by CIH-B's pre-existing spawn failure in McpTestClient::start (binary not found, every test panicked in fixture setup). Once CIH-B fixed binary resolution, the Coverage workflow surfaced the missing CursorStale. Slice is the minimal production fix: split PositionBeforeRetention into its own match arm that constructs ServiceError::CursorStale with both numeric fields; keep Sealed/IntegrityFailure/InvalidGap/Unavailable/Open in DrainFailed (Display formatting remains the legacy path).
